newsitem.title: USA: Alcan sees 1997 aluminum demand up 2.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: Alcan sees 1997 aluminum demand up 2.6 pct.

text.p: Alcan Aluminium Ltd now expects world aluminum consumption to increase 2.6 percent in 1997, its Director of Industry Analysis said Friday.
Roger Scott-Taggart told a news conference that would put demand at 24.565 million metric tonnes.
This, he continued, is based on the company's "preliminary numbers" showing 1996 consumption slipped 0.5 percent to 23.94 million tonnes from 1995's 24.06 million.
A year ago, he noted, Alcan saw a 1.6 percent increase in world consumption.

"The big surprise last year" was the decline in European consumption, Scott-Taggart said, adding Alcan now estimates European demand slipped 2.7 percent in 1996 and projects a 3.3 percent rise for this year.
North American demand, which the company had projected would be flat in 1996, is now estimated to have delined 1.7 percent, he said, adding a 1.6 percent rise is seen in 1997.

He said the "very strong turnaround" in aluminum prices in October and the recovery that continued until this week "may be more than restocking," adding Alcan's consumption projection of 1997 may prove to be conservative.
Scott-Taggart said Alcan now estimates that western world aluminum production increased six percent last year. Through November, it was up five percent to 15.75 million tonnes.
He said Russian exports rose 18 percent during the first 11 months of 1996 and Alcan estimates they were up 16 to 18 percent for the full year.
Some of last year's Russian export growth was taken up by an increase in Chinese imports, he said.
Stating Alcan is projecting flat Russian exports this year, Scott-Taggart said the company sees a Western World supply deficit of 250,000 tonnes.
Inventories remained level in 1996, with LME and producer inventories down just 60,000 tonnes for the year, he said.
